statement: Let n = len(nums). Say that a prefix ending at k is mergeable when 0 <= k < n and for every i with 0 <= i < k, nums[i] <= sum_{t=i+1}^{k} nums[t] (this condition is vacuous for k = 0). Let k0 be the largest such index k. The function returns a result r, and r = sum_{t=0}^{k0} nums[t]. Equivalently, r is the largest value of an element that can appear in the array after any finite sequence of the allowed merge operations.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: The function returns a result r on every input satisfying the preconditions; it does not overflow, panic, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), r >= nums[i].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= sum_{t=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[t].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an index k with 0 <= k < len(nums) such that r = sum_{t=0}^{k} nums[t].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an index k with 0 <= k < len(nums) such that: (1) for every i with 0 <= i < k, nums[i] <= sum_{t=i+1}^{k} nums[t]; (2) r = sum_{t=0}^{k} nums[t]; and (3) applying the allowed operation repeatedly inside the prefix 0..k collapses that prefix into a single element equal to r while leaving all elements after position k unchanged.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums) such that for all i with 0 <= i < k, nums[i] <= sum_{t=i+1}^{k} nums[t], we have sum_{t=0}^{k} nums[t] <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever len(nums) = 1 and the function returns a result r, r = nums[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever len(nums) = 2 and the function returns a result r, if nums[0] <= nums[1] then r = nums[0] + nums[1], otherwise r = nums[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] <= sum_{t=i+1}^{len(nums)-1} nums[t], the returned result r equals sum_{t=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[t].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever len(nums) >= 2 and nums[0] > sum_{t=1}^{len(nums)-1} nums[t], the returned result r equals nums[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] > nums[i+1], the returned result r equals nums[0].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let nums' be any slice obtained by appending one more element x to nums, where 1 <= x <= 1000000. If the function returns r on nums and returns r' on nums', then r' >= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) < 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.
